lines.trans: Lyova, please, do not even start.
Five minutes is not being late.
If the mustachioed walrus asks, I arrived on time.
Then you get a fine of half a paycheck.
Be late one more time and you will be left without a paycheck.
Lyova, but that is unfair!
And for the walrus comment, you are taking out the trash all day.
Now everything is fair, right?

wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record
meanings.note: Polite or pointed correction. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

выносить.gloss: to bear, to tolerate; to carry out

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'носить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to bear', forming an aspectual pair with 'вынести'.

examples.text: Ой, я совсем не выношу храп!
examples.trans: Oh, I cannot stand snoring at all!
Come on, let us bring the caviar into the hall.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
